perspective:
Keith’s available information:

- He works as a construction worker at a construction company where Elizabeth is the receptionist. They have a friendly but professional relationship through office interactions.
- Recently, he noticed Elizabeth had been unusually curt with him over the past few days.
- He wondered if he had done something to upset her, possibly through a misunderstanding or an unknown mistake.
- He asked Elizabeth if he had done something to upset her, saying she seemed off with him.
- He heard Elizabeth say no, not at all; she was dealing with personal stuff, and she apologized if she seemed short.
- He felt sympathetic and wanted to support her.
- He told her he understood she was going through a tough time, offered to listen, and suggested a coffee break.
- He heard Elizabeth accept the coffee break and thank him.
- During coffee, Elizabeth shared more about her stresses. Keith suggested she consider talking to a professional, saying an external perspective can help.
- He heard Elizabeth say she had thought about it but was hesitant about seeking help.
- He noticed Elizabeth became slightly withdrawn after his suggestion. He believed he might have embarrassed her and felt regretful.
- He told her he hoped he hadn’t overstepped and that he was there to support her no matter what.
- He heard Elizabeth say he didn’t overstep, she appreciated his concern, and it was a lot to think about.
- Afterward, Elizabeth seemed more open and appreciative to him. He believed she valued his support and felt more comfortable around him. He intended to maintain the supportive relationship.
- He told her he was glad they talked and that he is always available to chat or take a break.
- He heard Elizabeth thank him, say it meant a lot, and that she felt better knowing she had his support.
